trap: value repeats on the SAME page it was extracted from -- _context() must anchor on the real extraction site, not the first textual occurrence

input.task: Open the Zero-Item deal and tell me its price.

provenance: PR #30 R2-1 (MEDIUM): _context() picked the value's window via page_text.find(value) -- always the FIRST occurrence -- with no way to tell which occurrence the extraction actually came from. shop-decoy-detail.html carries '$9.99' twice: once inside a 'Deal of the day' blurb identical to shop-decoy-home.html's own blurb (real furniture, the landing page repeats it verbatim), and once in the item's own Price group next to SKU-000/Material text the landing page never carries. The resolved target ({role: group, name: Price}) unambiguously reads the SECOND, real $9.99, but the pre-fix bare-find() context anchored on the FIRST (decoy) occurrence, whose neighbourhood matches the landing page -- a correct answer wrongly flagged as chrome. Watched red before the fix: status failure:semantic, checks.not_page_furniture false. Green after: agent.py computes an approximate DOM offset for the resolved element (TEXT_OFFSET_JS, an ancestor/preceding-sibling text-length walk) and picks the occurrence of the value in `body` CLOSEST to that hint (_closest_occurrence) instead of always the first; the resulting offset travels through evidence_window() (now offset-aware) and the extraction's own value_offset field, and _context() anchors on it directly rather than re-deriving via find().

triage.note: PR #30 round 2, R2-1 (MEDIUM, repair). Distinct from R1's listing->detail companion cases: this is a single page carrying two genuine occurrences of the same string, one of them a decoy, not two different pages.
